entries.title: Indoor air can be dirtier than outside
entries.content: The EPA notes indoor air pollutant levels can be higher than outdoor levels. Controlling sources, airing out rooms and filtering air all help.
entries.source: An Office Building Occupant's Guide to Indoor Air Quality - EPA
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Keep vents clear
entries.content: Blocked vents and unserviced systems reduce fresh air. Keep grilles clear and report stuffy rooms.
entries.source: An Office Building Occupant's Guide to Indoor Air Quality - EPA
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Microplastics in indoor air
entries.content: A 2024 study measured tiny plastic particles in home and car air. Regular dusting, vacuuming and ventilation reduce indoor dust.
entries.source: Human exposure to PM10 microplastics in indoor air - PLOS One
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: New furniture and paint smells
entries.content: New furniture, paint and cleaners can release chemicals (VOCs) indoors. Choose low-emission products and air out rooms after renovating.
entries.source: An Office Building Occupant's Guide to Indoor Air Quality - EPA
entries.label: Evidence summary - education only

entries.title: Light and seasons at home
entries.content: Letting in natural daylight and fresh air supports a regular daily rhythm. Korea's five-color tradition also ties the home to the seasons.
entries.source: EPA Indoor Air Quality guide; Obangsaek guide
entries.label: Education + tradition
